chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Turayf. He said: 'Umayr ibn Ma'mun al-'Ataridi narrated to me. He said: I saw al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him)

he would sit in his place after praying Fajr until the sun rose. And I heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) say: Whoever prays Fajr then sits in his place remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rises, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will shield him from the Fire.

key_terms.الفجر: Fajr — the dawn prayer, the first of the five daily obligatory prayers
key_terms.ستره: Will shield/veil him — divine protection from the punishment of Hellfire
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific phrase glorifying God
key_terms.يذكر الله: Remembering Allah — engaging in dhikr, supplication, and glorification

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sitting in dhikr after Fajr prayer until sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a prophetic teaching narrated through Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (AS), who was personally observed by 'Umayr ibn Ma'mun practicing this devotion. The Prophet (SAWW) promised that one who prays the dawn prayer and remains seated in their place of worship engaged in dhikr (remembrance of God) until sunrise will be shielded from the Hellfire. The triple repetition of the promise emphasizes its certainty and the great reward attached to this practice, which was common among the earliest Muslims as a form of extended worship in the blessed early morning hours.
